0.value:
mgl_orientation_disks draws rotations as rings, so an orientation can be seen rather than read.

A rotation is three or four numbers and you cannot read it. A ring lying in the plane of the rotation, as large as the rotation is, you can: the direction it faces is the axis, and its size is how far it has turned.

THE DATA:
'axis-angle' takes one row per disk. A row of three is a rotation vector - its direction is the axis and its length the angle in radians - and the disk is drawn facing along that axis with a radius of the angle times 'scale'. A row of four is an axis followed by a size, and the radius is that size times 'scale'. A disk with no rotation is not drawn. Rows beyond the node's disk count are ignored.

A single disk can be sent as a flat row, [x y z] or [x y z size]: a flat list is read as one row.

WHERE THEY APPEAR:
All the disks are drawn at the same place - the origin of the chain's current coordinates - one over another. To put a set at a joint, use a transform before it, or patch it to mgl_body's joint_callback; or use mgl_body_orientation, which draws a set at every joint at once.

COLOURS:
Each disk has its own colour, sent to 'color 0', 'color 1' and so on as red green blue alpha from 0 to 1. The colours glow regardless of lighting, and the defaults are translucent so overlapping rings show through each other.

'ring_width' is the ring's width as a fraction of its radius - 1 fills the disk in. 'slices' sets how round it is.

SYNTAX:
mgl_orientation_disks
mgl_orientation_disks <count> <scale> <slices>

All optional: 6 disks, scale 0.5, 32 slices.

EXAMPLE:
mgl_orientation_disks 3 0.25

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

mgl chain in:
The chain. 'draw' draws the disks.

scale:
Radius per radian (or per unit of size, for four-number rows).

slices / ring_width:
Roundness, and ring width as a fraction of the radius. 0.1 by default.

axis-angle:
One row per disk, as above. It is kept until new rows arrive.

color 0, color 1 ...:
One inlet per disk, red green blue alpha.

OUTPUTS:

mgl chain out:
The chain, continuing.

RELATED:
mgl_body_orientation draws these at every joint of a body. gl_orientation_disks is the older equivalent.
